feed.title: Towards A K-of-N Lightning Network Node

entry.title: Towards A K-of-N Lightning Network Node
entry.summary:
A comprehensive draft detailing the signer group design can be found at [this link](https://github.com/davelund110/bolts/blob/39c63a434a3bf8add47f5812fc550f20d5e89ca8/signer-group-design-note.md). This document is structured in alignment with the requirements-only version of lightning-blake2b/bolts17 and delves into multiple core aspects critical to secure and robust digital signature systems.
The design encapsulates the management of keys and secrets, specifically utilizing VPSS1 over replicated PRF keys. Each signer within the system maintains distinct records and adheres to a well-defined set of operational rules to ensure consistency and security. Revocation procedures are articulated as a three-round process involving participation from all N signers, which contributes to fault tolerance and collective decision-making.
Procedures for closing are described to allow any K out of N signers, including scenarios where a previously restored signer participates. The mechanism for splicing, as well as handling nonces, is thoroughly explored, reflecting attention to both flexibility and cryptographic soundness.
Several open questions remain, particularly regarding the agreement step analogous to Iceberg’s protocol. There is a focus on whether it suffices for signers to only sign versions explicitly named by all participants when N is greater than or equal to 2K − 1, or if it becomes necessary to adopt Iceberg’s threshold of N ≥ 3K − 2 for stronger guarantees. These unresolved considerations invite further expert feedback to determine the optimal balance between efficiency and security in multi-party signing protocols.
